body.text: Why should all walking tours happen BEFORE your hair transplant day?

All strenuous walking, crowded landmarks, and steep climbs belong before surgery because newly implanted hair grafts are not secure during the first two weeks and the scalp remains tender and swollen for several days. Front-loading sightseeing lets you enjoy Istanbul comfortably without risking accidental head bumps, heavy sweating, or sunburn.

The [NHS hair transplant recovery guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/) stresses extra care for the first two weeks because grafts are not yet secure, while the [ISHRS post-operative overview](https://ishrs.org/after-hair-restoration-surgery/) notes one to two days of mild discomfort followed by seven to ten days of scalp tenderness. Front-loading Sultanahmet, Galata, and bazaar walks removes crowd-bump risk and leaves calm time to meet your treating doctor in person—a key step highlighted in [ISHRS patient guidance](https://ishrs.org/top-5-things-to-know-about-hair-transplantation/).

body.text: What calm activities (private Bosphorus boat, hotel terrace) work post-op?

Once your clinic completes your Day +1 check and confirms you are fit for light movement, calm seated activities with shade and minimal walking work best: a private enclosed-cabin Bosphorus boat, a quiet hotel terrace overlooking the strait, or a short chauffeured scenic drive. Keep outings brief and avoid midday heat.

A private Bosphorus boat with a shaded salon lets you see Dolmabahçe Palace and waterfront mansions without stairs, ferry queues, or direct sun. A hotel room with a Bosphorus terrace also makes resting upright effortless.

Which activities (hamam, sun exposure, swimming, dusty bazaars) are strictly off-limits?

Turkish baths (hamam), saunas, steam rooms, swimming pools, sea bathing, direct sunlight, vigorous exercise, and crowded or dusty bazaars are strictly off-limits immediately after a hair transplant. Heat, sweat, chlorinated or open water, UV rays, and airborne dust increase infection risk and can disturb delicate grafts.

The [NHS hair transplant guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/) cautions against touching grafts when bandages come off around days two to five and advises cutting down exercise in the first month. Book any hamam visit on Day -2 before surgery—never afterward.

items: Skip heat and steam: No hamam, sauna, hot tub, or uphill walks.
Avoid direct sun: Stay shaded; skip tight caps unless your surgeon explicitly approves one.
Zero swimming: Avoid pools and sea water until clinically cleared.
Avoid crowds and dust: Skip packed trams and dusty bazaar alleys.
Watch car roofs: Use high-roof vehicles so your scalp never grazes a doorframe.

body.text: How do you schedule hotel check-in around Day 1 surgery?

Check into your Istanbul hotel at least two nights before surgery day so you finish walking tours, recover from flight fatigue, and keep the exact same room through post-op discharge. Request extra pillows for propped-up sleeping, quiet upper-floor rooms, and early breakfast service on surgery morning.

Keeping one continuous hotel stay from pre-op sightseeing through your first clinic wash avoids moving luggage while bandaged and swollen. Build a calm buffer night before flying home, in line with [CDC Yellow Book medical tourism planning advice](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html). faq.q: How many nights should I plan for a hair transplant plus Istanbul sightseeing?
faq.a: Five to six nights works well: two to three pre-op nights for walking tours, surgery day, and two calm post-op nights for dressing removal and rest.

faq.q: Can I visit a Turkish hamam after my hair transplant?
faq.a: No. Steam, heat, sweat, and scrubbing are off-limits during early healing. Schedule a hamam before surgery day instead.

faq.q: Is a Bosphorus boat ride safe two days after surgery?
faq.a: Only if your clinician clears light outings and you book a private boat with a shaded, wind-sheltered cabin rather than crowded public ferries.

faq.q: Can I wear a baseball cap while sightseeing post-op?
faq.a: Tight hats can rub or dislodge fresh grafts. Avoid headwear unless your surgeon explicitly approves a specific loose option and timing.

faq.q: When can I wash my hair and fly home?
faq.a: Bandages often come off around days 2 to 5 with gentle hand washing around day 6, depending on your clinic's protocol. Confirm flight clearance with your medical team.
